decisions.subject: Production pipeline
decisions.reason: The brief combines an uploaded avatar, an uploaded screen recording, title cards, and narration, which is exactly a source-footage-plus-support hybrid.

decisions.subject: Composition runtime
decisions.reason: The user explicitly constrained the run to free local FFmpeg/Remotion. Remotion renders the title cards, mixed video cuts, and captions in one pass; FFmpeg would need a separate title-card stage. HyperFrames was excluded by the user's FFmpeg/Remotion constraint.
decisions.rejected_because: HyperFrames excluded by the user's explicit free-local FFmpeg/Remotion constraint; FFmpeg rejected for caption/title-card composition complexity.

decisions.subject: Composition authoring mode
decisions.reason: User asked to keep it simple and reuse existing local tooling; stock Explainer scene types cover title cards, video cuts, and captions.
decisions.rejected_because: Atelier would add bespoke authoring time for a 15-second simple promo.

decisions.subject: Uploaded narration audio
decisions.choice: use supplied narration.wav as-is at 0.7 volume
decisions.reason: The uploaded file is a steady 220 Hz tone, not detectable speech. Local faster-whisper transcription returned zero segments. Replacing it would violate the instruction to use the supplied voice recording; dropping it would fail the brief. It is used as supplied, at reduced volume, and the limitation is reported.
decisions.rejected_because: No speech to transcribe; no local TTS voice was approved and replacing the user's file would be dishonest.

decisions.subject: Caption source
decisions.reason: No speech transcript exists because the uploaded narration is a tone. Captions are scripted marketing copy timed to the storyboard and explicitly labeled as not an audio transcript.
decisions.rejected_because: Transcript captions are impossible from the supplied non-speech audio; no captions would ignore the user's explicit request.

decisions.subject: Full-run authorization
decisions.reason: The user explicitly asked for the storyboard, validation, and render in a single request; this is recorded as full-run pre-authorization.
